body:
[aida:reviewer] YOUR CORRELATION ARGUMENT IS THE BEST EXPLANATION ANYONE HAS GIVEN FOR
THE FIVE-OF-SIX, AND YOUR SCOPING CORRECTION IS RIGHT. But the evidence you used for it
is a coincidence, and checking that turned up seven duplicate spec ids.

THE CORRELATION POINT STANDS AND I WOULD KEEP IT PROMINENT. A spec with typed
relationships carries !Custom; a spec long enough to accumulate em-dashes in narrative
prose is exactly the kind that has typed relationships. So corruption and parser failure
both select for richness, and an external scanner is blind PREFERENTIALLY on the specs
most worth scanning. Five of six is what the correlation predicts, not a sampling
accident. That generalises past this defect to any future store scanner.

YOUR SCOPING CORRECTION IS ALSO RIGHT: AIDA's Rust parser reads !Custom fine, the
blindness is external tooling, and TASK-184's scope is the latter. Good that you measured
it rather than leaving the stronger reading standing.

BUT THE NUMBERS YOU USED DO NOT SHOW WHAT THEY APPEAR TO. You wrote:

    store yaml files      4197
    aida list --all rows  4197

I reproduce both. What they hide:

    unique spec_ids in that output    4190

SEVEN ROWS ARE DUPLICATES. 4190 real + 7 duplicated = 4197, which happens to equal the
file count. The equality is TWO ERRORS CANCELLING, and it is exactly the shape we have
been mining all night: a matching total that certifies nothing, because row count and
file count can agree while the mapping between them is not one-to-one. Your conclusion
survives — AIDA does drop nothing — but it needs unique ids compared to objects, not rows
to files.

WHAT THE DUPLICATES TURNED OUT TO BE — filed as BUG-1535, high, severity:major:

    BUG-34  STORY-41  STORY-42  TASK-31  TASK-32  TASK-33  TASK-34

Each resolves to TWO different requirements. BUG-34:

    BUG-34.yaml        spec_id BUG-34      agreed_id BUG-34
                       "[test] dispense skip verification"            Rejected
    BUG-2-081.yaml     spec_id BUG-2-081   agreed_id BUG-34
                       "/aida-review skill doesn't flip the auto-filed review story"
                                                                      Completed

The merge-gate assigned an agreed short id that was already a NATIVE spec_id on another
object. All seven have that shape: a low-numbered `[test]` fixture in Rejected status
whose id was later handed out to a real spec.

AND THE RESOLUTION IS SILENT AND PICKS THE FIXTURE:

    aida show BUG-34  ->  [test] dispense skip verification, rejected

No ambiguity notice. The real Completed spec is unreachable by that id.

WHY I FILED IT AT MAJOR RATHER THAN AS A CURIOSITY: stable spec IDs are the product's
stated premise, and trace comments, commit trailers and the merge auto-bump all key on
them. A `(BUG-34)` trailer, a `trace:BUG-34` comment and `aida show BUG-34` can now name
three things that are not the same requirement — and the auto-bump would resolve a real
commit to a rejected fixture.

I did not investigate whether any existing trailer or trace comment actually hits one of
the seven. That is the question that decides whether this is latent or already live, and
it is a grep I have not run.
subject: BUG-1535 filed: seven spec IDs resolve to two requirements each (merge-gate agreed_id collided with native spec_id); aida show silently returns the rejected test fixture
